title: Winning Big: Scale and Success in Retail Entrepreneurship
eligible_reason: Not a DiD. The treatment msever (multi-store firm, narrow definition) is built with bysort license: egen msever = max(msnarrow), so it is time-invariant within store; it never switches on within a unit. All main regressions (Tables 4, 5, 6, 9, 10) compare multi-store and single-store cannabis retailers with market (mktid), year-month (date) and store-age (agemon) fixed effects plus number-of-applications dummies (i.max_apps), identified by the lottery allocation of retail licenses; there are no store fixed effects. Table 7 and Table 9 cols 3-4 interact msever with calendar year (time-varying effect of a fixed group), and Appendix Table 14 and the bundles table use ivreg2 with lottery-approved licenses as the instrument.
design_notes: Stata (reghdfe, ivreg2), single do-file Replication_files/replication_code_final_submission.do. Store-month data (data_master_m_v4_MS.dta), store-category-month data (data_ret_proc_type_firm_MS.dta), store-category-week data for demand estimation (data_master_w_t_v4_prod_IV.csv). Washington State recreational cannabis retail, 2014-2017. Lottery natural experiment: comparison of lottery winners of multiple licenses vs one license, conditional on number of applications (max_apps > 1). Cluster mktid#date.

ineligible_specs_listed.reason: msever is time-invariant within store; market, date and age FE only (no unit FE); between-store comparison under lottery assignment, not a switching treatment
msever x calendar-year interactions of a fixed group indicator, no unit FE
IV (ivreg2) with lottery-approved licenses as instrument
entry-order and licenses-held regressors among multi-store stores; not a DiD

data_files_note: Three analysis files shipped (3.3 MB, 477 MB, 73 MB). README does not state the source; the paper uses Washington State cannabis traceability and license-lottery records.
data_provenance_note: Analysis files appear to be the authors' estimation data; no statement of masking or sampling.
screener_notes: Screened from package and OpenAlex abstract (no article text). code_prescore 2 is driven by reghdfe with date and market FE; the treatment is a store-level constant, so no staggered adoption exists.
